statement: Convert a string s into a 32-bit signed integer, the way the C function atoi does, but read the digits with recursion instead of a loop and without any built-in conversion.

First skip any leading spaces. Then an optional '+' or '−' sign sets the sign, positive if there is none. Then read digits until a non-digit character or the end of the string; if no digit is read the value is 0. Leading zeros do not change the value.
The recursion builds the value one digit at a time: the value of the digits up to position i is 10 × (the value up to position i − 1) + the digit at i.
Apply the sign. If the result is above 2³¹ − 1 return 2³¹ − 1, and if it is below −2³¹ return −2³¹. Otherwise return the result.

examples.explanation: The space is skipped, '−' makes the number negative, and the digits 0, 4, 2 build the value 42, so the result is −42.
Reading stops at the space after 4193; the words that follow are ignored.
The value −91283472332 is below −2³¹, so it is clamped to −2147483648.
